fields.title: Settings shows the Internal Work Orders toggle, off, with its description
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
fields.custom_steps: 1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A toggle "Internal Work Orders" shows on the tab, written in Title Case like the other toggles.
  • The toggle is off.
  • Its description reads "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S1-R1: “Settings > Work Orders shows a toggle "Internal Work Orders" (Title Case like the other toggles on the tab), off by default, organization-wide like the other toggles, with the description "Lets you flag your own company as an internal customer and mark a customer's work order, or a single line of a billable work order, as No Charge (warranty, goodwill, comeback). Internal and no-charge work orders close without an invoice; their parts cost posts to the expense account of their category instead of Cost of Parts."”
  • Feature Overview: “Two kinds of work order, one way to close them.”
  • Terminology: “Internal Work Orders → the name of the setting under Settings > Work Orders and of the report under Reports; both cover internal and no-charge work orders, as does the Technician Efficiency chip "Internal work orders: Hide / Only internal / Show all" (tooltip "Internal and no-charge work orders", S9-R3). On a flagged customer's work order the badge reads Internal, never No Charge.”

S1-02.section_name: Turn on Internal Work Orders, internal customers and categories
S1-02.title: First turn-on opens the customer picker window with Save disabled
S1-02.automation: AUTOMATION: Not available on Build to test Yet - Last checked 11/12/2026

fields.title: First turn-on opens the customer picker window with Save disabled
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  2. Switch the "Internal Work Orders" toggle on.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The toggle "Internal Work Orders" is off.

Step 2:

  • A window titled "Which customers are your own company?" opens.
  • It has a customer picker with search, and no customer is picked.
  • Under the picker the hint reads "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer."
  • The line "You can change this any time: Customers > Edit Customer > Internal customer." shows.
  • It has the buttons "Do this later" and "Save"; "Save" is disabled.
  • The window lists no customer as already flagged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories)

  • S1-R2: “Switching the toggle from off to on for the first time in the organization opens the modal "Which customers are your own company?" with the body "Work orders for these customers are internal: no prices and no invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of their category when you use QuickBooks or AccountingHub. Nothing is picked for you: your location is not always a customer, and the names can differ. Pick one or more, or do it later from the customer page.", a customer picker (the standard customer Select with search, several customers can be picked, each shown as a chip with a remove control; up to 50, with the hint "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer."), the line "You can change this any time: Customers > Edit Customer > Internal customer." and the buttons "Do this later" and "Save". No customer is preselected. Save is disabled until at least one customer is picked. Save saves the toggle (on) and flags the picked customers in one step (only this toggle and the flags; other unsaved changes on the tab wait for Save settings; to back out, the user switches the toggle off and saves settings), closes the modal and then shows the dialog of S1-R11 for each picked customer with open billable work orders, one after another; the page shows the toggle on and the hint lines of S1-R3 with nothing left to save for this setting. Closing the modal with X acts as "Do this later" (S1-R5); Esc and a click outside do nothing, as in every dialog of the app. The modal is shown once per organization: switching the toggle on again later opens nothing (S1-R10). Switching it off opens nothing. The modal never lists who is flagged, and Settings > Work Orders never lists customers.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “First-time modal, more than 50 customers | "Pick up to 50 customers here. Flag more from Edit Customer." | Hint under the customer picker (S1-R2)”
  • Story 1, Entry points: “Not on New Customer, not in a Settings list and not on the work order itself: a work order becomes internal only through its customer. Removing the flag: unticking the checkbox (S1-R6), allowed any time with the info dialog of S1-R12. Who is flagged is visible on the Customers list and the customer header (S1-R8), not in Settings.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

fields.title: Picking two customers and Save turns the setting on and flags both
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization in which the Internal Work Orders setting has never been switched on.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A with no open work orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B with no open work orders.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open Settings > Work Orders.
  2. Switch the "Internal Work Orders" toggle on.
  3. Type customer A's name in the customer picker.
  4. Pick customer A.
  5. Type customer B's name in the customer picker.
  6. Pick customer B.
  7. Click Save.
  8. Open the Customers list.

Expected Result

  • The toggle is off.

Step 2:

  • The "Which customers are your own company?" window opens.

  • Customer A is offered.

  • Customer A shows as a chip with a remove control.
  • "Save" becomes enabled.

Step 5:

  • Customer B is offered.

  • Customer B shows as a second chip with a remove control.

Step 7:

  • The window closes.
  • The toggle shows on.
  • The hint lines show under the description.
  • Nothing is left to save for this setting: leaving the page asks nothing about unsaved changes for it.

Step 8:

  • Customer A and customer B each show an "Internal" badge next to their name.

It is shown while the setting is on (S1-N4 for the exception). New Customer does not show it: a customer is flagged after it exists, from Edit Customer or the modal. The checkbox and the modal are the only places the flag is set; ticking it on Save flags the customer (with the dialog of S1-R11 when open billable work orders exist).”
  • S1-R8: “While the setting is on, a flagged customer shows an "Internal" badge next to its name in the customer header, in the customers list and on the customers list mobile card. While the setting is off the badge is hidden in all three places (S1-N4); the badges on work orders stay (S2-R10).”
  • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • Key Decisions, Permissions (Action | Needs | Without it): “See the Internal badge on the customers list and the customer header | Customers page access | Not applicable”
  • Terminology: “Internal customer → one of the shop's existing customers flagged as the shop's own company or a sister company. Set in the modal that opens the first time the setting is switched on, or at the bottom of Edit Customer; nowhere else. Several allowed. Not a system customer: ShopView creates nothing.”
  • Feature Overview: “Internal work orders come from internal customers. The shop flags its own company (and any sister company) as an internal customer once: in the modal that opens the first time the Internal Work Orders setting is switched on (nobody is preselected: the location is not necessarily a customer and the names differ), or later with the Internal customer checkbox at the bottom of Edit Customer. Settings > Work Orders holds the toggle, that one-time modal and two hints: a link to the categories page and a link to the QuickBooks mapping. Every internal customer carries a default internal category, General Internal unless changed on Edit Customer; an asset of an internal customer can carry its own category (Edit Asset).   • S1-R11: “When a customer is flagged (Save in the modal, or on Edit Customer with the checkbox ticked), or the setting is turned on again while flagged customers have open billable work orders (S1-R10), a dialog reads "[n] open work orders for [customer] are billable. Make them internal? Prices, fees and discounts are removed; costs and hours are kept." and lists those work orders under the body, one line each (number, location, unit, status), at every location the user has access to, up to 10 rows and then "and [n] more". Counted as open: every billable work order of that customer that is not invoiced, not paid and not Declined, Estimates included. A row with a deposit carries the note "Deposit: stays billable"; a row with a posted vendor bill carries the note "Vendor bill: cost moves at Close" (no dialog of S2-R8 per work order on this path). Buttons: "Keep billable" and "Make internal". Make internal applies S2-R7 to every listed work order without a deposit; those with a deposit stay billable until the deposit is reversed and the dialog is shown again. Keep billable leaves them as they are; they finish with an invoice as today. Open no-charge work orders of that customer are not listed: they stay no charge with their category and keep Change category and Convert to Billable (S2-R6). With no open billable work orders the dialog is not shown. Saving Edit Customer for a customer that carries the flag shows this dialog again whenever that customer has open billable work orders, so work orders left billable earlier (a deposit since reversed, Keep billable, a user without 'Work Orders — Create & Edit') can be made internal later. Open billable work orders at locations the user has no access to are not listed; the line "[n] more at locations you don't have access to." under the list says how many, and they are converted when a user with access saves Edit Customer or the setting is turned on again (S1-R10). Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. A pending portal estimate of a work order made internal is no longer available: the portal refuses approval with "This estimate is no longer available." and shows the existing obsolete banner, since internal work orders are never on the portal (S2-R11).”
  • S2-R7: “Changing the customer on a work order works as today (not offered on an invoiced or paid billable work order, as today, nor on a closed internal or no-charge work order, S2-R9); until then the classification follows the new customer: to an internal customer the work order becomes internal (prices removed, costs and hours kept, no Convert actions); to a regular customer from an internal one it becomes billable (lines priced as in S2-R6). A No Charge mark and its category survive a change to another regular customer; a no-charge work order moved to an internal customer becomes internal and loses its category. The Change Customer dialog says what will happen to the prices and, when the work order stays internal or no charge, adds "Shop supplies resets to [customer]'s minimum ($[amount])." (without 'See Financial Data' the sentence omits the amount).”
  • Key Decisions: “Flagging a customer offers to make its open billable work orders internal; removing the flag is free and leaves open internal work orders internal.”
  • S2-R13: “The classification is written on the work order when it is created, when its customer changes and when it is converted; the closed record carries it too, with the category. Lists, reports and integrations read it from there, never from the customer flag. Converting to no charge or to billable, changing the category, a shop supplies amount change, Make internal (S1-R11, on each work order), Close with its posting date, Reopen, and adding or removing a customer's Internal flag are recorded in the work order or customer Audit Log with the user and the time.”

fields.custom_steps: 1. Open Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The page has two tabs, Internal categories and No Charge categories.
  • The Internal categories tab shows the columns Category, QuickBooks expense account (with the green QuickBooks mark), Internal customers using it, and Work orders.
  • General Internal is listed with a "Default" badge.
  • Each row has a menu with Edit and Archive.
  • The buttons "New Internal Category" and "New No Charge Category" show.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11758 (Story 1, Turn on Internal Work Orders, flag internal customers, manage categories), story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S1-R13: “Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders is a page with two tabs. Internal categories: columns Category (the default carries a Default badge), QuickBooks expense account (with the QuickBooks mark; "Not set" with a warning icon when empty), Internal customers using it, Work orders (count, all time; a billable work order with a no-charge line of the category counts too), and a row menu with Edit and Archive. No Charge categories: Category, QuickBooks expense account, Original work order (Required / Not asked), Work orders, row menu. Buttons "New Internal Category" and "New No Charge Category". The starting set is seeded for every organization when this release ships, so the categories, the QuickBooks rows (S5-R5) and the hub rows (S6-R2) exist before the setting is turned on; turning the setting on seeds nothing: General Internal (default, cannot be archived); Warranty (requires the original work order), Goodwill (does not), Comeback (requires). Archived categories stay on the work orders and lines that used them and in the report filter under Archived; a "Show archived (n)" link lists them with Restore. The page needs 'Settings — Service', like every Administration > Service page; while the setting is off it shows the notice "Internal Work Orders is off. Turn it on in Settings > Work Orders." and the lists stay editable. Each list holds up to 100 active categories; past that, the New button is disabled with "You can have up to 100 active categories in this list. Archive one to add another." The QuickBooks expense account column is shown only while the current location is connected to QuickBooks.”
  • S1-R16: “A category has a stable key; renaming it keeps the history, the report filter and the mappings. Archiving a category in use keeps it on existing work orders, lines, documents and reports; it is no longer offered in any select. The default Internal category cannot be archived; changing the default moves nothing on existing customers. The green QuickBooks mark (the existing QuickBooks icon) is shown wherever a field maps to QuickBooks: the account columns and pickers of S1-R13 and S1-R14, the asset field of S1-R15 and the Settings hint of S1-R3. Archiving a category that is the stored default of customers or assets first shows "[n] internal customers and [m] assets use this category as their default. Their new work orders will use the next category in line." The stored value stays on the customer and the asset, shown as "[name] (archived)" with the hint "Archived. Pick an active category."; resolution for a new work order (S2-R1) skips archived categories: the asset's, else the customer's, else the default Internal category, the first active one wins. Restore puts everything back as it was.”
  • Terminology: “Category → a shop-managed entry in one of two lists on Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders: Internal categories (where the cost of work on the shop's own equipment goes) and No Charge categories (why a customer's work order or line is free). Each carries a QuickBooks expense account per location and, on No Charge, whether it requires the original work order. Replaces "reason".”
  • Key Decisions: “Categories are shop-managed and carry the account; the work order never asks an accounting question. The category of an internal work order is resolved from the asset, else the customer, else General Internal; a no-charge category is picked where No Charge is set.”

  • S2-R1: “In the New Work Order dialog, picking a customer with the Internal customer flag shows the "Internal" badge next to the customer name with an info icon; the tooltip reads "Internal customer: no prices, no invoice. There is no checkbox to tick and no category to pick on the work order. The work order is created internal with the category resolved as: the asset's Internal category (S1-R15), else the customer's default (S1-R7), else the default Internal category; it is re-resolved while the work order is open when the asset changes or when the category of the asset or the customer is edited (a closed work order never changes), archived categories are skipped (S1-R16), and it can be changed on the asset or the customer, never on the work order.   • S2-N3: “If the selected customer is an internal customer, the "No Charge" checkbox is not shown in the New Work Order dialog and a billable work order of that customer offers no Convert action (S2-R2, S2-R7). Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R2: “In the New Work Order dialog (New Work Order only; Edit Work Order, which shares the dialog, is unchanged), picking a customer without the flag shows, at the bottom of the dialog below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and separated from it by a divider, an unticked checkbox "No Charge" with an info icon whose tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." Ticking it reveals the required select "Category" listing the active No Charge categories, empty by default; Save is refused with the field message "Pick a category" until one is picked. When the category requires the original work order, the select "Original work order" appears under it (the customer's invoiced and closed work orders at the locations the user has access to, those on the same asset first, each as number, date and first line, and "Not in ShopView" under Other), optional here, with the helper "Which earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView, and the line on it. The line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers. Optional here, required at Close."; once a work order is picked, the optional select "Original line" lists its lines (number, title, technician). The checkbox is hidden when the selected customer is an internal customer and for users without 'See Financial Data'. Ticked, the work order is created No Charge with that category. It works whether or not any customer is flagged. As soon as a work order or a line is picked, the line "Original technician: [names]" (or "Original technician: none") shows under the selects, so a wrong attribution is seen and corrected by picking the line before anything is saved.”
  • S2-R17: “When the category requires the original work order, every dialog that sets the category (New Work Order S2-R2, Convert to No Charge S2-R5, Change category S2-R6, and the line dialogs of Story 12) shows the selects "Original work order" and "Original line" of S2-R2. Both are optional in the dialogs; the original work order is required at Close (S3-R2) and before Create invoice on a no-charge line (S12-R9); "Not in ShopView" satisfies it. The original technicians are derived when saved and stored with the work order or the line: every technician the original line shows, however they were assigned, by hand or from a schedule shift (a line with several technicians gives several, and the comeback counts once for each in the report); without an original line, the technician assigned to the original work order; without one, or with "Not in ShopView", none, and the report shows the job under Unassigned so it stays in the totals. They are shown in the dialog as soon as the original is picked, in the report (S9-R2) and in the hub record (S8-R1). The original work order is a link on the document, in the notes and in the report.”

  • The header card has an orange outline and a light orange background.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R3: “The work order header shows one badge next to the status: "Internal" for an internal work order, "No Charge" for a no-charge work order (a different style from Internal), in the desktop and the mobile header. It is the only mark on the work order: the customer card on the detail page shows no badge and no category. On the detail page the header card of an internal or no-charge work order has an orange outline and a light orange background (a new style for the header card, on desktop and on the mobile header; the design authority names the token), so the work order is recognised at a glance; there is no hint sentence under the header. The category of a no-charge work order is not shown on the work order; it is in the Change category dialog, on the NO CHARGE document and in the report (S2-R16). A billable work order that carries no-charge lines carries no badge and no header style; the line carries the mark (Story 12).”
  • Feature Overview: “Both look and work like a normal work order until the end. Estimates, approvals, parts ordering, picking, receiving, clocking and the review step work exactly as today. Lines show quantity, cost and hours and no sell prices: no labor rate, no part price, no totals, no tax, no fees, no discounts. Shop supplies is one flat amount (below). Nobody zeroes anything. One badge, "Internal" or "No Charge", shows next to the status wherever the work order appears, and on the detail page the header card is outlined in orange so nobody invoices it by habit.”

You can convert it to no charge again until it is invoiced." and the buttons Cancel and "Convert to Billable"; confirming removes the badge and the category and prices every line the way a new line on this work order would be priced that day: labor at the customer's labor rate, else the location's; parts from the pricing rules applied to the cost already on the line (the cost Close would post), not today's catalogue cost. Change category opens the dialog "Change category for work order [number]" with the Category select (the current category preselected) and, when the new category requires it, the Original work order and Original line selects of S2-R2 (changing to a category that does not require them clears them) and the buttons Cancel and Save; Save is enabled once the category, the original work order or the original line differs from the current values (as on a line, S12-R5), so a missing original can be added before Close; it changes nothing else. It is offered while the setting is off too (S2-N1). Cancelling or dismissing any of these leaves the work order as it was. From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R3: “Confirming completes the work order if it is not yet Complete, creates the internal invoice underneath (carrying the work order number, nothing owed), relabels the picks to the internal invoice and sends their journal entries as invoicing does today (parts leave stock when they are picked), posts the entries of Stories 7 and 8, and shows the alert "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." (or "Closed · No Charge."), with the X every alert in the app has. The work order shows the status Closed with its one badge (Internal or No Charge) and is locked as an invoiced work order is; underneath, the internal invoice is in the Closed state (Key Decisions). Every other effect of invoice creation applies: the snapshot in the work order history, the search index, the audit log; the exceptions are the ones listed in S3-R4 and the Customer PO rule of S3-R5. Adding a line to a closed work order spawns a new work order, as it does on an invoiced one today; the new one takes its customer's classification (S2-R1) and is billable on a regular customer. When the work order is not yet Complete, Close first runs the same completion steps as Create invoice today (tech stories, cores, and the missing details such as VIN, mileage and engine hours, per the organization's settings); the last button of that run reads "Close Work Order" and opens the confirmation of S3-R2.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Closed | "Work order [number] is Closed · Internal." | Success alert, fades on its own, with the X every alert has”
  • Key Decisions: “Under the hood, Close creates an invoice marked internal or no charge. The screen says Closed · Internal or Closed · No Charge.”
  • Terminology: “Closed · Internal / Closed · No Charge → how running text, the Close confirmation, the success alert and the Reopen dialog name a closed internal or no-charge work order. On screen the status reads Closed and the one badge next to it reads Internal or No Charge, so the classification shows once. Underneath it is a work order with an internal invoice in the Closed state; the locks of an invoiced work order apply.”
  • Terminology: “Statuses are named as the app names them: Estimate, Approved, In Progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid and Declined. This feature adds the label Closed, which only the internal invoice carries underneath (Key Decisions); Authorization is a line status, not a work order status.”

Expected Result

Step 1:

Step 2:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 3:

Step 4:

  • The Finance tab shows the document and no payment, balance or $0 payment.

Step 5:

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order)

  • S3-R4: “No payment is recorded (not even the $0 payment a $0 invoice writes today) and no "Invoice paid" log entry is written, no customer transaction or receivable is created, no customer portal notification, email or invoice webhook is sent (the work order status webhook of Story 11 is), no invoice is sent to QuickBooks, the internal invoice is never listed in the Open API invoice lists and invoice.created and invoice.paid are never sent for it (both from the core release on, before Story 11), no tax, fee or discount is added, the shop supplies amount is not charged to the customer (it posts as an expense, Story 10), and the customer portal does not list the document (the portal vehicle list still counts a closed internal or no-charge work order for Last Service and Completed, as a service on the unit with $0.00 owed). Close and Reopen are recorded in the work order log as invoice created and reversed are today.”
  • S3-R6: “The asset Invoices tab lists the closed work order with status Closed, the badge, Total balance "No Charge" and Discount and Tax rate empty (rows on that tab have no actions). Customer statements, the customer balance and credit limit checks do not include it, and no message driven by an open balance can pick it up, since it carries none. The Finance tab menu of the closed work order offers Reopen Work Order only (S4-R1); Issue Credit is not shown, as there is nothing to credit.”

  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S5-R1: “Integrations > QuickBooks, ShopView Accounts, shows one row per category directly under Cost of Parts (above Cost of Goods (tax)), grouped under the headers "Internal work orders" and "No Charge work orders", each row named after its category and carrying the QuickBooks mark. A category the shop adds appears as a new empty row; an archived category keeps its row, greyed, with its mapping, and the row can still be remapped (a reopened work order still posts to its archived category, S12-E8). Under the rows a note reads "Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are credited to the income account of your Shop supplies item in Products And Services; nothing to map here." Nothing is created in QuickBooks: the picker lists the location's existing expense accounts.”
  • S10-R5: “No new mapping row in either integration: QuickBooks credits the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) (Story 5, S5-R1 note); AccountingHub uses its existing "Shop supplies expense" row (Story 6).”
  • Terminology: “Category expense account → the expense account mapped to a category per location: one ShopView Accounts row per category in QuickBooks (S5-R1), one Account Mappings row per category in AccountingHub (S6-R1). Replaces the two fixed rows Internal Work Orders Expense and Customer No-Charge Expense of v0.17.”
  • Feature Overview: “Accounting is one expense account per category. In QuickBooks the accountant maps each category once per location, on the category itself or on the ShopView Accounts page, where the categories show as one row each under Cost of Parts; an empty row posts to ShopView Review as every unmapped row does today, with no fallback to another row. In AccountingHub, Account Mappings holds one row per category, automatically mapped for the starting categories (General Internal to 6500 Vehicle Expenses; Warranty and Goodwill to the existing 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense; Comeback to 6440 Comeback Expense). The rollout migration and new-customer setup reuse suitable accounts, create missing required accounts, preserve valid existing mappings and resolve number conflicts with an available number, so all starting mappings are ready before the first job posts (S6-R2); a category the shop adds gets an empty row that holds the event until it is mapped; an archived category keeps its row. The shop supplies credit is unchanged (Story 10). At Close of a whole internal or no-charge work order the parts cost debits the category's account and the credit stays on today's inventory account by part category and stock location. On a billable work order with a no-charge line, that line's parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created; the rest of the work order posts as today.”
  • Key Decisions: “One expense account per category, mapped per location in QuickBooks (as every ShopView Accounts row is) and per organization in AccountingHub (as every Account Mappings row is), with the starting categories mapped automatically in the hub (S6-R2).”

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11763 (Story 6, AccountingHub account mapping)

  • S6-R2: “Automatically set up the starting category mappings using AccountingHub's existing chart of accounts. General Internal defaults to 6500 Vehicle Expenses, already in the default chart. Warranty and Goodwill both default to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense, already in the newer chart. Comeback defaults to 6440 Comeback Expense, a new required account (number confirmed by the AccountingHub owner on 2026-11-09). The existing 6400 Shop Equipment Maintenance account remains available for accountants to select where appropriate; it is not an additional starting category. The mapping key should allow a kind (parts, labor) later, so V2 adds rows instead of changing the contract.”
  • Feature Overview: “Accounting is one expense account per category. In QuickBooks the accountant maps each category once per location, on the category itself or on the ShopView Accounts page, where the categories show as one row each under Cost of Parts; an empty row posts to ShopView Review as every unmapped row does today, with no fallback to another row. In AccountingHub, Account Mappings holds one row per category, automatically mapped for the starting categories (General Internal to 6500 Vehicle Expenses; Warranty and Goodwill to the existing 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense; Comeback to 6440 Comeback Expense). The rollout migration and new-customer setup reuse suitable accounts, create missing required accounts, preserve valid existing mappings and resolve number conflicts with an available number, so all starting mappings are ready before the first job posts (S6-R2); a category the shop adds gets an empty row that holds the event until it is mapped; an archived category keeps its row. The shop supplies credit is unchanged (Story 10). At Close of a whole internal or no-charge work order the parts cost debits the category's account and the credit stays on today's inventory account by part category and stock location. On a billable work order with a no-charge line, that line's parts cost posts to the category's account when the invoice is created; the rest of the work order posts as today.”

  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.

fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • Two inventory journal entries are found, one per stock part, numbered as invoicing numbers them today.
  • Part A's entry debits account X $80.00 (2 × $40.00) and credits the inventory account the invoice would credit for that part's category and stock location.
  • Part B's entry debits account X $25.00 and credits its inventory account.
  • Nothing is debited to Cost of Parts.
  • Together they post $105.00, the Stock parts figure of the confirmation, with no invoice: no month-end reclass is needed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R2: “At Close, ShopView sends the inventory journal entries it sends at invoice today (one per picked stock part, same numbering, dated the posting date), with the debit on the expense account of the work order's category instead of the part category's cost of goods sold account or Cost of Parts, and the credit on the same inventory account the invoice would credit today (by part category and stock location). Each entry's memo carries the work order number, the classification and the category. Today these entries are sent only after the QuickBooks invoice synced; Close sends them on its own, with no invoice. The QuickBooks Class of the entry comes from the location of the work order (the mapping the location already uses for its other entries), not from a labor line's labor-rate mapping, which an internal work order does not have; without a Class on the location the entry is sent without one, as today for a part without a labor rate.”
  • Key Decisions: “Part cost goes straight to the expense account, not to cost of goods sold first, one entry per part as invoicing posts today.”
  • Goals: “For a shop on QuickBooks Online or AccountingHub, the month-end reclass journal entry for internal and no-charge jobs is no longer needed.”
  • Terminology: “Category expense account → the expense account mapped to a category per location: one ShopView Accounts row per category in QuickBooks (S5-R1), one Account Mappings row per category in AccountingHub (S6-R1). Replaces the two fixed rows Internal Work Orders Expense and Customer No-Charge Expense of v0.17.”

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S8-R3: “Vendor bill lines, reclass entries and the shop supplies entry follow Story 7, S7-R3, S7-R3a, S7-R4 and S7-R4a, with the hub's accounts (the credit goes to the Shop supplies expense row, seeded 5100 Shop Supplies COGS: in the hub the amount lowers cost, where in QuickBooks it raises shop supplies income; gross and net profit come out the same in both, and the accountant can remap the row). A vendor bill or vendor credit line on internal or no-charge work posts to the category's expense account (Key Decision); when that category row is empty, the bill or credit posts as today, so the vendor can be paid, and only that line's move to the category account is Held with the reason "No Charge: [Category] row not mapped" (or "Internal: [Category] row not mapped") until the row is mapped. This is the one entry the hub raises itself instead of receiving it from core (confirmed by the hub owner on 2026-11-09), with this lifecycle: when the mapping is saved, the Held move is retried automatically, subject to the other posting checks, an open accounting period included; a bill or credit amended while the move is Held turns it Dismissed and the updated document is evaluated again, with a replacement move only when one is still needed; a bill or credit voided while Held turns it Dismissed with no replacement; a bill or credit amended or voided after the move posted reverses the original move and posts an updated one when needed, coordinated with the bill or credit correction so the same amount is never reversed twice; Held moves can be retried, Dismissed ones are never replayed (S4-R3); the move shows in reconciliation and on the Accounting Events page with its status and a link to the source bill or credit and its line. Invoices, vendor bills, credits and payments keep today's statuses.”
  • S10-R4: “At Close, the amount posts as one entry: debit the work order's expense account (the expense account of the work order's category), credit the shop supplies account (Story 7, S7-R4a; Story 8, S8-R3). Reopen reverses it (Story 4).”
  • Terminology: “Shop supplies account → where the shop supplies amount of an internal or no-charge work order is credited: in QuickBooks the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) (mapped today for billable invoices; no new row), in AccountingHub the existing Shop supplies expense row.”

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

Invoices, vendor bills, credits and payments keep today's statuses.”

The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11761 (Story 4, Reopen a closed internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11765 (Story 8, AccountingHub, the closed work order and its parts cost)

In QuickBooks, Reopen reverses only what was posted at Close, to the same accounts (S7-R5): an entry posted to the mapped account or to ShopView Review gets its reversal; an entry never sent (S7-N5) gets none; an entry still waiting in QB Unexported gets none, and its row is marked "Withdrawn: work order reopened". An entry Marked as Exported by hand counts as posted (S7-E2).”
  • S8-E2: “If a work order is reopened while its Close event is Held, the Held event is withdrawn and no reversal is posted (Story 4, S4-E1).”
  • S4-R3: “Confirming reverses exactly the entries that were posted at Close (Stories 7 and 8), returns the parts to inventory as Reverse does today, removes the internal invoice, and sets the work order to Complete with its classification unchanged, the shop supplies amount kept, and the Convert and Change category actions offered again (S2-R9 applies only while closed or invoiced). The reversal is dated the reopen date, so it is held only if that date's period is closed or missing (S4-E2 is corrected accordingly). Events for one work order are processed in order, one at a time: a Reopen arriving while the Close is Held turns the Close Dismissed; a Dismissed event is never retried and cannot be replayed by hand; a new Close waits while an earlier reversal for the same work order is Held, shown as Held with the reason "Waiting for an earlier held entry of work order [n]", so two Close entries are never posted without the reversal between them. The reversal credits and debits exactly the accounts the Close used.”

  • S9-R1: “Sales, Sales By Customer, Sales By Representative and Advisor Analysis leave whole internal and no-charge work orders out of every number, with no filter and no option to include them. Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R2: “The report "Internal Work Orders" under Reports lists the closed internal and no-charge work orders of the organization and, one row each, the no-charge lines of invoiced billable work orders. Filters: date range on the posting or invoice date (default this month, at most 12 months), Location (all or one), Classification (All / Internal / No Charge / No Charge line), Category (All or one, archived under a heading), Original technician (All or one). Above the table a summary strip shows one card per category in the range: parts cost, count of work orders and lines, hours. Two tabs. "By work order and line", columns: Work order (link), Line ("Whole work order", or the line number and title), Customer, Classification, Category, Original work order (link, with the original line number when set), Original technician, Closed / invoiced (the posting date, or the invoice date for a line), Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, as on the NO CHARGE document, S3-R5; for a line, its own parts), Shop supplies (empty on a line), Hours (the labor hours on the lines, as on the document; clocked hours per technician are in Technician Efficiency with Only internal); a totals row for the whole range, not the page; rows sorted by date, newest first. "By technician", one row per technician with the columns Completed lines (lines with status Complete in the range on which the technician clocked time, the definition Technician Efficiency uses, so the two reports agree), Comeback lines and Warranty lines (no-charge lines of those categories whose stored original technicians include this technician, S2-R17), Comeback rate (comeback lines / completed lines), Redo hours and Redo parts cost (the hours and parts cost of that comeback and warranty work). A whole no-charge Comeback or Warranty work order counts as one line in this tab, with all its hours and parts cost. A line with several technicians counts once for each of them, in the numerator and the denominator, hours and cost shown whole for each; the totals row counts every line once; a note under the table says so. A row "Unassigned" holds the work without an original technician (Not in ShopView, or no technician on the original). The dollar cost of labor arrives with labor posting. Export: the PDF carries both tabs as sections with the same columns; the CSV carries the tab that is open, as every export gives what is on screen.”
  • Terminology: “Internal Work Orders → the name of the setting under Settings > Work Orders and of the report under Reports; both cover internal and no-charge work orders, as does the Technician Efficiency chip "Internal work orders: Hide / Only internal / Show all" (tooltip "Internal and no-charge work orders", S9-R3). On a flagged customer's work order the badge reads Internal, never No Charge.”

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R3: “Technician Efficiency shows a filter chip "Internal work orders: Hide / Only internal / Show all" (the existing single-choice chip; the chip covers internal and no-charge work orders, tooltip "Internal and no-charge work orders"), default Show all, on both the Invoiced and the Completed tab, so internal hours count as work from the start. From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S10-R1: “An internal or no-charge work order carries one field "Shop supplies" (a dollar amount) in the block where a billable work order shows its totals. It is set when the work order becomes internal or no charge: the customer's Min shop supplies charge from the customer profile, or $0.00 when none is set. The percentage rule and the location percentage do not apply. On a flagged customer, Edit Customer accepts the Min without a shop supplies percentage (today Min is disabled until a percentage is entered); a percentage, if set, never applies to internal or no-charge work orders.”
  • Feature Overview: “Shop supplies are a flat amount. An internal or no-charge work order carries one Shop supplies amount, defaulted from the customer's Min shop supplies charge and editable on the work order until Close. At Close it posts as one entry: debit the work order's expense account, credit the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services) in QuickBooks, or the existing Shop supplies expense row in AccountingHub. No new mapping row for it. No percentage in this version.”
  • Key Decisions: “Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders are a flat amount, defaulted from the customer's Min shop supplies charge, posted at Close as a debit to the work order's expense account and a credit to the account the shop already maps for shop supplies: in QuickBooks the income account of the existing "Shop supplies" item (Products And Services), in AccountingHub the existing Shop supplies expense row.”

Make internal converts the listed work orders without switching location. fields.title: Parts cost is the same in the confirmation, document, report and QuickBooks
fields.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure General Internal is mapped to account X at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with 2 stock parts at $40.00 ($80.00), one special-order part billed at $125.00 after the work order was internal, 2.0 labor hours and Shop supplies $15.00.
fields.custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. Open the Finance tab.
  5. Open Reports > Internal Work Orders.
  6. In QuickBooks Online, open the entries on account X for work order 1.
fields.custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation shows "Stock parts $80.00" and "Special orders and sublet $125.00".

Step 3:

  • The work order is Closed.

Step 4:

  • The document reads "Parts cost $205.00" ($80.00 + $125.00).

Step 5:

  • Work order 1's row reads Parts cost $205.00.

Step 6:

  • Account X carries $80.00 from the Close and $125.00 from the bill: $205.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync), story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S3-R2: “Close opens the confirmation "Close work order [number]?" with a posting date field (default today; it follows the rules of Invoice Date on the Finance-tab Create invoice today, and it is the date of the internal invoice, of every entry, and of the record in every report, export and the asset Invoices tab) and these rows: "Stock parts $[stock parts cost]" with the note "Posted to [mapped account name]" (the amount reads "$[amount], includes $[core amount] core cost" when a picked part carries a core, S2-E7); "Special orders and sublet $[amount]", one line per state present: already posted to the work order's account (note "Already posted to [account] at the vendor bill"), posted elsewhere and reclassed at Close (note "Moved from [account] to [account]"), and not yet billed (note "Posts to [account] when the vendor bill is entered"); the amount is the vendor bill line amount for billed items and the line cost for items not yet billed; the row is hidden when there are none; "Labor [hours] h" with the note "Hours only, nothing posted"; "Shop supplies $[amount]" with the note "Posted to [work order's expense account], credited to [shop supplies account]" (row hidden when the amount is $0.00). The document and the report show one Parts cost: stock parts plus special orders (S3-R5). Under the rows: "This posts the parts cost and shop supplies to your books and marks the work order Closed · Internal. You can reopen it later." when the work order is already Complete, or "This completes the work order, posts the parts cost and shop supplies to your books and marks it Closed · Internal. You can reopen it later." when it is not (Closed · No Charge on a no-charge work order). Buttons: Cancel and "Close Work Order". Parts cost is the cost on each line at Close, as invoicing posts to Cost of Parts today; the hours are the labor hours on the lines. With both QuickBooks and AccountingHub, each note names the QuickBooks account and the AccountingHub account. When the category requires the original work order and none was picked, the confirmation shows the select "Original work order *" (and "Original line") above the rows with the warning "[Category] requires the original work order. Pick the earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView."; Close Work Order stays disabled until one is picked; Goodwill never shows this. The Stock parts note names the category's account ("Posted to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense").”
  • S3-R5: “The Finance tab of a closed work order shows the NO CHARGE document: the masthead as on the invoice today (letterhead left, the shop logo in the centre slot, the document block "Internal Work Order [number]" or "No Charge Work Order [number]" with the date right), and under the masthead line, on the left and never over the logo, the INTERNAL or NO CHARGE stamp with the line "Category: [name]" and, when set, "· Original work order [number]" (a link in ShopView, plain on the PDF), Bill to the customer, the asset block, labor lines with hours only, parts lines with quantity and cost only (cost under 'See Financial Data'), a Summary with Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, at the amounts of S3-R2, core cost excluded, S2-E7), Shop supplies (when above $0.00) and Labor hours (the labor hours on the lines), and no tax, total, payments, balance or signature block; with Download, Print and Email (the recipient field is empty; the user types the shop's own address or any other; never automatically). The Customer PO field is not required. The internal invoice carries the work order number, as every invoice does today; no number is consumed or skipped. Parts cost on the document and in the report is fixed at Close: a vendor bill entered, edited or deleted after Close posts its own amounts to the work order's expense account (S7-R3) and changes neither the document nor the report. Email uses the invoice email template of today (it carries no amounts) with the subject "Internal Work Order [number]" or "No Charge Work Order [number]".”
  • S9-R2: “The report "Internal Work Orders" under Reports lists the closed internal and no-charge work orders of the organization and, one row each, the no-charge lines of invoiced billable work orders. Filters: date range on the posting or invoice date (default this month, at most 12 months), Location (all or one), Classification (All / Internal / No Charge / No Charge line), Category (All or one, archived under a heading), Original technician (All or one). Above the table a summary strip shows one card per category in the range: parts cost, count of work orders and lines, hours. Two tabs. "By work order and line", columns: Work order (link), Line ("Whole work order", or the line number and title), Customer, Classification, Category, Original work order (link, with the original line number when set), Original technician, Closed / invoiced (the posting date, or the invoice date for a line), Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, as on the NO CHARGE document, S3-R5; for a line, its own parts), Shop supplies (empty on a line), Hours (the labor hours on the lines, as on the document; clocked hours per technician are in Technician Efficiency with Only internal); a totals row for the whole range, not the page; rows sorted by date, newest first. "By technician", one row per technician with the columns Completed lines (lines with status Complete in the range on which the technician clocked time, the definition Technician Efficiency uses, so the two reports agree), Comeback lines and Warranty lines (no-charge lines of those categories whose stored original technicians include this technician, S2-R17), Comeback rate (comeback lines / completed lines), Redo hours and Redo parts cost (the hours and parts cost of that comeback and warranty work). A whole no-charge Comeback or Warranty work order counts as one line in this tab, with all its hours and parts cost. A line with several technicians counts once for each of them, in the numerator and the denominator, hours and cost shown whole for each; the totals row counts every line once; a note under the table says so. A row "Unassigned" holds the work without an original technician (Not in ShopView, or no technician on the original). The dollar cost of labor arrives with labor posting. Export: the PDF carries both tabs as sections with the same columns; the CSV carries the tab that is open, as every export gives what is on screen.”
  • S7-R2: “At Close, ShopView sends the inventory journal entries it sends at invoice today (one per picked stock part, same numbering, dated the posting date), with the debit on the expense account of the work order's category instead of the part category's cost of goods sold account or Cost of Parts, and the credit on the same inventory account the invoice would credit today (by part category and stock location). Each entry's memo carries the work order number, the classification and the category. Today these entries are sent only after the QuickBooks invoice synced; Close sends them on its own, with no invoice. The QuickBooks Class of the entry comes from the location of the work order (the mapping the location already uses for its other entries), not from a labor line's labor-rate mapping, which an internal work order does not have; without a Class on the location the entry is sent without one, as today for a part without a labor rate.”
  • S7-R3: “When a vendor bill is created for a special-order part or a sublet on a work order that is already internal or no charge, the bill line posts to the mapped expense account instead of Cost of Parts (or the category account); the vendor, the bill and Accounts Payable are unchanged. This covers the bill of a vendor-bought job entered as a special-order part (sublet, Terminology) and the vendor's core charge (S2-E7).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close), story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S3-N1: “If the work order is billable, the button reads "Create invoice" and everything works as today.”

  • S7-R8: “On a billable work order with no-charge lines (Story 12), the invoice is sent to QuickBooks as today with those lines at $0.00. For each no-charge line, the inventory journal entries of its picked stock parts debit the line's category account instead of Cost of Parts, with the same credit, numbering, dating and idempotency as S7-R2 and S7-R6; special orders and sublet on the line follow S7-R3 and S7-R4 with the category account. The billable lines post as today. Invoice reversal reverses them with the rest. The no-charge line is sent on the QuickBooks invoice as a line: the same labor and part items it would carry as a billable line, its quantities, price 0.00, the same tax code (tax is zero on zero), and the category name in the description, so the QuickBooks invoice reads like the PDF. The cost reaches the category account through the journal entry, never through the invoice. Vendor bills per line: a bill entered while the line is No Charge posts the line to the line's category account (S7-R3 per line); a line marked No Charge after its bill posted is reclassed from Cost of Parts to the category account when the customer invoice is created (S7-R4 per line); Mark as Billable after a bill posted to the category account reclasses back to Cost of Parts at invoicing; Create invoice has no confirmation today (SV-10312), so when at least one vendor bill's cost will move at invoicing and the location has an accounting integration, Create invoice first opens "Create invoice [number]?" with one "Moved from [account] to [account]" row per move and the buttons Cancel and "Create invoice"; every other Create invoice runs as today, with no dialog. The Class rule of S7-R2 applies. The API owner confirms how today's $0 statement of a declined line is sent and makes the no-charge line the explicit case.”
